issues.description: Contradictory instructions about the SealSaloon.stock attribute: the problem text first instructs students to initialize a final Stock stock in the constructor (per-instance final), but later explicitly requires that the stock attribute must be static (shared across all instances). A static final field cannot be initialized in an instance constructor. This contradiction will confuse students about whether stock should be an instance-level final field initialized in the constructor or a static final field initialized at declaration/static initializer.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent: either (A) require an instance-level final Stock stock and instruct students to initialize it in the constructor (remove the static requirement), or (B) require a static final Stock stock and instruct students to initialize it at declaration or in a static initializer. Update the problem text and UML to match the chosen approach (and update example code accordingly).

issues.description: Method name/signature mismatch for the supply-delivery operation: the problem statement UML and the template Main call the static method acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int), but the reference solution implements a static method named receiveDelivery(String, int, int). This name mismatch between spec/template and solution (and sample Main) is structural and will confuse students about the correct API to implement and use.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent method name and signature across the problem statement, template Main, and solution. Preferably align the solution with the specification and template Main by implementing a static acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity) method (or update the spec and Main to call receiveDelivery if that name is preferred). Ensure the chosen name is reflected in UML, examples, and tests.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies a static SealSaloon method named acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int) to handle incoming ingredient deliveries, but the solution implementation defines a static method named receiveDelivery(String, int, int). This inconsistent naming for the same conceptual operation (accepting/receiving a supply delivery) creates a mapping barrier: students reading the problem will implement or look for acceptSupplyDelivery, while the reference solution and likely tests use a different identifier, causing confusion and potential test mismatches.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the solution method receiveDelivery(String, int, int) to acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int) (keeping it static) so that the method name matches the problem statement and student expectations. Alternatively, update the problem statement to use receiveDelivery everywhere if that name is preferred; both artifacts should use the same identifier.
